newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Consob meets, Olivetti on agenda.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Consob meets, Olivetti on agenda.

text.p: Italy's stock market watchdog Consob met on Monday evening and is expected to set an agenda for meetings related the accounts of troubled high-tech group Olivetti.
A Consob source said the meeting was a routine one but "it should also discuss the week's calendar related to Consob's activity regarding the situation of Olivetti's accounts."

The bourse watchdog said on Friday night after Olivetti issued a statement defending its accounting practices and saying its figures for the first six months were in order that it would continue its investigation of Olivetti's accounts and planned to meet the company's auditors this week.

Consob said then it had not made a full and detailed examination of Olivetti's first-half figures but had made sure the company's statement contained enough information to allow its shares to resume trading today after a two day suspension last week.
But Olivetti shares collapsed on the Milan stock exchange today after the suspension was lifted, forcing exchange authorities to step in again and halt trading.

The crisis-hit group's stock price slid to below 600 lire, triggering an automatic suspension in the afternoon under exchange rules limiting price movements to 20 percent either way, the stock market council said.
Trading failed to start again and dealers said it was now expected to get underway again on Tuesday morning.
